identity.title: A second post-AGB nebula that contains gas in rotation and in expansion: ALMA maps of IW Carinae

paper_type_evidence.quote: We obtained high-quality ALMA observations of $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO $J$=3$-$2 lines in IW Car.

evidence.quote: Following those authors we adopt a distance of 1 kpc for this source, but we stress that this value is uncertain.
Following those authors we adopt a distance of 1 kpc for this source, but we stress that this value is uncertain.

question.value: Are rotation (Keplerian disk) and expansion (outflow) both present in the post-AGB nebula around IW Car, and what are its mass, central stellar mass and disk lifetime?

evidence.quote: We aim to study the presence of both rotation and expansion in post-AGB nebulae, in particular around IW Car
We made use of the ALMA dataset ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00338.S.
$\lambda$ = 0.8 mm, obtained with ALMA, receiver band 7.
We present maps of IW Car in the $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO $J$=3$-$2 lines

with an array configuration of 42 antennas providing baselines between 12 and 1572 m.
leading to a resolution (HPBW) of approximately 0$''$17$\times$0$''$ 17.
In total, $\sim$ 110 minutes of acquisitions were obtained on source.
Four tracks were consecutively observed on July 26, 2015

what.value: Model nebula built on properties derived for 89 Her and the Red Rectangle

evidence.quote: we base our modeling on the properties we previously derived for those objects.

what.value: X(13CO) ~2e-5 adopted to compare with previous results

analysis_steps.goal: Map the emission and measure morphology

method.value: Channel maps and position-velocity diagrams along the equatorial direction (PA -15 deg)

evidence.quote: Figs. 4 and 5 show position-velocity diagrams along the direction perpendicular to the outflow axis, which corresponds to the equatorial plane, at –15$^\circ$.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit simplified LTE model of CO emission

method.value: Parametric nebula with Keplerian disk plus radial hourglass outflow, power-law density and temperature, compared to maps

evidence.quote: The density and temperature ($n$ and $T$) are assumed to depend solely on the distance to the center and the equator with potential laws.

key_parameters.value: V(2e15 cm)=2.5 km/s; inclination ~45 deg (±15); X(13CO)~2e-5; X(12CO)~1e-4

evidence.quote: We adopt a value of $\sim$ 45$^\circ$ ($\pm$ 15$^\circ$).
We assume LTE populations for the involved rotational levels.

validation.value: Comparison of synthetic and observed channel maps and p-v diagrams

evidence.quote: The model reproduces most of the observed features, but some problems are still present.

method.value: Total mass from fitted model; lifetime from outflow kinematical time and mass-loss rate

findings_qualitative.value: Hourglass-like expanding outflow with axis perpendicular to a Keplerian rotating equatorial disk

evidence.quote: expansion, which shows an hourglass-like structure with a symmetry axis perpendicular to the rotation plane

claims.hypothesis: IW Car hosts both a rotating disk and an expanding outflow
claims.experiment: ALMA 12CO/13CO J=3-2 maps and p-v diagrams
claims.result: Hourglass lobes and Keplerian pattern detected
claims.finding: Both components are present, the outflow likely extracted from the disk

evidence.quote: Our observations clearly show the presence of gas components in rotation, in an equatorial disk, and expansion

claims.hypothesis: Disk and outflow masses and central mass can be estimated
claims.result: Mtot~4e-3 Msun, outflow ~8x lighter than disk, M*~1 Msun

evidence.quote: the outflow is approximately eight times less massive than the disk.

why_this_method.value: Data S/N and resolution moderate and only two lines mapped, so a simplified model is used

evidence.quote: Under these conditions, very detailed models, as those developed for the Red Rectangle, are not sensible and we only perform simplified modeling.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Constant velocity modulus, axial expansion and expansion parallel to the equator rejected

evidence.quote: We can exclude some other simple cases, such as constant velocity modulus, expansion in the axial direction, and expansion parallel to the equator

limitations_admitted.value: ~25% flux filtered out, model overpredicts faint extended emission

evidence.quote: a small fraction of $\sim$ 25% of the flux has been filtered out in the maps of $^{12}$CO $J$=3$-$2.
The axis inclination with respect to the plane of the sky is poorly determined

referee_caveats_inferred: Mass depends mainly on assumed X(13CO) and distance of 1 kpc
